hypotheses.reasoning: order-consumer processed orders.events batches normally (e.g. #1924 at 05:46:42, lag ~100ms) until msg-577362 at offset 589882 (partition 1) arrived. Its payload has a NUL byte at position 902, so JSON parse fails on every attempt (#1932, #2110, #2196, #2308). The consumer has no max-retry or dead-letter configuration, so the message is nacked and redelivered forever (attempt 9 at #1937, attempt 13 at #2112). Partition 1 is blocked behind it and lag climbs from 606 msgs/68s (#2095) to 8124 msgs/396s (#2674). CPU is normal because the consumer is spinning on retries, not computing. The single GC pause (#854) is not the cause.

Not the cause of the orders.events lag. catalog-svc's translation API rejects credentials with 401 invalid_api_key, which points to an expired or rotated key. This explains the search 502 cascade (#2002, #2021) and is a separate incident, listed only because it is the other high-severity fault in the window.

verdict.recommendedAction: Move msg-577362 (offset 589882, partition 1) to a dead-letter queue or skip it manually to unblock partition 1, then add a max-retry limit with DLQ routing to order-consumer. Investigate the upstream producer that wrote a NUL byte into the order payload, and validate or sanitize payloads at produce time. Verify lag drains once unblocked. Separately, open a ticket for the translation API 401s in catalog-svc (likely an expired or rotated API key), which are breaking search (search-api and web-bff 502s). Metrics-agent queue drops are a secondary symptom.

The consumer has no max-retry or dead-letter configuration, so the message is nacked and redelivered forever (attempt 9 at #1937, attempt 13 at #2112). Partition 1 is blocked behind it and lag climbs from 606 msgs/68s (#2095) to 8124 msgs/396s (#2674). CPU is normal because the consumer is spinning on retries, not computing. The single GC pause (#854) is not the cause.

Not the cause of the orders.events lag. catalog-svc's translation API rejects credentials with 401 invalid_api_key, which points to an expired or rotated key. This explains the search 502 cascade (#2002, #2021) and is a separate incident, listed only because it is the other high-severity fault in the window.

input.recommendedAction: Move msg-577362 (offset 589882, partition 1) to a dead-letter queue or skip it manually to unblock partition 1, then add a max-retry limit with DLQ routing to order-consumer. Investigate the upstream producer that wrote a NUL byte into the order payload, and validate or sanitize payloads at produce time. Verify lag drains once unblocked. Separately, open a ticket for the translation API 401s in catalog-svc (likely an expired or rotated API key), which are breaking search (search-api and web-bff 502s). Metrics-agent queue drops are a secondary symptom.
